content.question: What is the key difference between discriminative and generative models?
options: Discriminative models require more training data, while generative models work without any data.
Discriminative models generate new data samples, while generative models classify inputs into categories.
Discriminative models learn the conditional probability of the output given the input, while generative models model the joint distribution of input and output and can generate new samples.
Discriminative models capture the underlying structure of the inputs, while generative models ignore it.
content.answer: Discriminative models learn the conditional probability of the output given the input, while generative models model the joint distribution of input and output and can generate new samples.
